from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions", [
            "Vectors represent movements or directions in space.",
            "We can scale vectors to stretch or shrink them.",
            "Adding scaled vectors creates a linear combination.",
            "For example, three steps East and two steps North.",
            "This operation combines basic movements into new paths."
        ])

        # Colors
        color_a = "#FFD700"  # Gold/Yellow
        color_b = "#00BFFF"  # Deep Sky Blue
        color_res = "#ADFF2F" # GreenYellow

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_a)
        
        # Vector A: East (1 step) starting at D2
        origin = self.grid["D2"]
        target_a = self.grid["D3"]
        vector_a = Arrow(origin, target_a, buff=0, color=color_a)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=color_a).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "E3") # Positioned within 1 unit
        
        self.play(Create(vector_a), Write(label_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_a)
        
        # Stretch to double length (k=2)
        target_2a = self.grid["D4"]
        label_ka = MathTex("k \cdot A", color=color_a).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_ka, "E4")
        
        self.play(
            vector_a.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, target_2a),
            Transform(label_a, label_ka)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Flip West (k=-1)
        target_minus_a = self.grid["D1"] # West from D2
        self.play(
            vector_a.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, target_minus_a)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_res)
        
        # Cleanup first part
        self.play(FadeOut(vector_a, label_a))
        
        # Show A (East) and B (North)
        vector_a_new = Arrow(origin, self.grid["D3"], buff=0, color=color_a)
        label_a_new = MathTex("A", color=color_a).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a_new, "E3")
        
        vector_b = Arrow(origin, self.grid["C2"], buff=0, color=color_b)
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=color_b).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "C1")
        
        self.play(Create(vector_a_new), Create(vector_b), Write(label_a_new), Write(label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(color_res)
        
        # Scale to 3A and 2B
        target_3a = self.grid["D5"]
        target_2b = self.grid["B2"]
        
        label_3a = MathTex("3A", color=color_a).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_3a, "E5")
        
        label_2b = MathTex("2B", color=color_b).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_2b, "B1")
        
        self.play(
            vector_a_new.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, target_3a),
            vector_b.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, target_2b),
            Transform(label_a_new, label_3a),
            Transform(label_b, label_2b)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Tip-to-tail: Move 2B to end of 3A
        # New origin for 2B is D5. 2 units North from D5 is B5.
        target_tip_to_tail = self.grid["B5"]
        
        self.play(
            vector_b.animate.put_start_and_end_on(target_3a, target_tip_to_tail),
            label_b.animate.move_to(self.grid["B6"]) # Adjust label position
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Resultant vector
        resultant = Arrow(origin, target_tip_to_tail, buff=0, color=color_res)
        label_res = MathTex("3A + 2B", color=color_res).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_res, "A4")
        
        self.play(Create(resultant), Write(label_res))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(color_res)
        
        # Final highlight
        self.play(Indicate(resultant))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the scene
        title = "The Span: Reaching Every Corner"
        lines = [
            "- The span is the set of all reachable points.",
            "- Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane.",
            "- One vector alone only spans a single line."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_A = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        COLOR_B = "#00BFFF"  # Sky Blue
        COLOR_SPAN = "#404040" # Dark Grey
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Update lecture line color
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT))
        
        # Vector A from D3 to D5 (horizontal)
        vec_a = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D3"], 
            end=self.grid["D5"], 
            buff=0, 
            color=COLOR_A,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=COLOR_A)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Vector B from D3 to B3 (vertical)
        vec_b = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D3"], 
            end=self.grid["B3"], 
            buff=0, 
            color=COLOR_B,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=COLOR_B)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_a), Write(label_a))
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_b), Write(label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        # Span Plane - Represented by a filled area
        span_plane = Rectangle(
            width=5.0, height=5.0, 
            fill_color=COLOR_SPAN, 
            fill_opacity=0.4, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        self.place_in_area(span_plane, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Scatter of dots to visualize linear combinations filling the space
        np.random.seed(42)
        origin_x, origin_y = self.grid["D3"][0], self.grid["D3"][1]
        dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(
                point=[
                    origin_x + np.random.uniform(-2, 3), 
                    origin_y + np.random.uniform(-2, 3), 
                    0
                ],
                radius=0.04,
                color=COLOR_SPAN
            ) for _ in range(200)
        ])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(span_plane), FadeIn(dots))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        # Remove vector B and the plane visuals to focus on A
        self.play(
            FadeOut(vec_b),
            FadeOut(label_b),
            FadeOut(span_plane),
            FadeOut(dots)
        )
        
        # Span of a single vector A is a line
        span_line = Line(
            start=self.grid["D1"],
            end=self.grid["D6"],
            color=COLOR_A,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(Create(span_line))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup: reset lecture line color
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Trap", [
            "Linear dependence means one vector is redundant.",
            "It can be formed by combining other vectors.",
            "Redundant vectors do not expand the existing span."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        color_a = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        color_b = "#00BFFF"  # Deep Sky Blue
        color_c = "#FF4500"  # Orange Red
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_a))
        
        # Define vectors A and B
        # Origin at D2
        origin = self.grid["D2"]
        pos_a = self.grid["D4"]
        pos_b = self.grid["B2"]
        
        vec_a = Arrow(origin, pos_a, buff=0, color=color_a)
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{A}", color=color_a).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "E4")
        
        vec_b = Arrow(origin, pos_b, buff=0, color=color_b)
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{B}", color=color_b).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "B1")

        # Span area
        span_rect = Rectangle(
            width=2, 
            height=2, 
            fill_opacity=0.2, 
            fill_color=WHITE, 
            stroke_width=1,
            stroke_color=WHITE
        )
        span_rect.move_to((origin + self.grid["B4"]) / 2)
        
        self.play(Create(vec_a), Write(label_a))
        self.play(Create(vec_b), Write(label_b))
        self.play(FadeIn(span_rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_c))
        
        pos_c = self.grid["B4"]
        vec_c = Arrow(origin, pos_c, buff=0, color=color_c)
        label_c = MathTex(r"\vec{C}", color=color_c).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "A5")
        
        self.play(Create(vec_c), Write(label_c))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show C = A + B by shifting B
        vec_b_copy = vec_b.copy()
        self.play(
            vec_b_copy.animate.put_start_and_end_on(pos_a, pos_c).set_stroke(opacity=0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Formula A + B = C
        # Consolidate into a single MathTex call to resolve LaTeX compilation issues
        formula = MathTex(
            r"\vec{A}", "+", r"\vec{B}", "=", r"\vec{C}",
            tex_to_color_map={r"\vec{A}": color_a, r"\vec{B}": color_b, r"\vec{C}": color_c}
        ).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "F3")
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_b))
        
        # Highlight that C is inside the span_rect
        self.play(span_rect.animate.set_fill(color_b, opacity=0.4))
        self.play(Indicate(span_rect))
        self.play(Wiggle(vec_c))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Linear Independence: The Essential Team", [
            "Linearly independent vectors provide unique, essential directions.",
            "No vector in the set depends on the others.",
            "Adding an independent vector increases the dimension spanned."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show vectors 'A' (East, #FFD700) and 'B' (North, #00BFFF) on a 2D plane.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Define base origin and vector endpoints
        origin_pos = self.grid["E2"]
        vec_a_pos = self.grid["E5"]
        vec_b_pos = self.grid["B2"]
        
        vector_a = Arrow(origin_pos, vec_a_pos, color="#FFD700", buff=0)
        vector_b = Arrow(origin_pos, vec_b_pos, color="#00BFFF", buff=0)
        
        label_a = MathTex("A", color="#FFD700").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "F5")
        label_b = MathTex("B", color="#00BFFF").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "B1")
        
        # Create a parallelogram representing the span (plane)
        span_plane = Polygon(
            origin_pos, vec_a_pos, self.grid["B5"], vec_b_pos,
            color=WHITE, stroke_width=1, fill_opacity=0.1
        )
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_a), GrowArrow(vector_b))
        self.play(Write(label_a), Write(label_b))
        self.play(FadeIn(span_plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Introduce vector 'D' in #ADFF2F pointing 'Up' out of the plane.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Simulate 3D "Up" with a diagonal vector
        vec_d_pos = self.grid["C4"]
        vector_d = Arrow(origin_pos, vec_d_pos, color="#ADFF2F", buff=0)
        label_d = MathTex("D", color="#ADFF2F").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_d, "C5")
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_d))
        self.play(Write(label_d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Expand the 2D plane into a translucent 3D volume (cube) to show the new span.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Define vertices for the volume (parallelepiped)
        # v0: Origin, v1: A, v2: B, v3: D
        v0 = origin_pos
        v1 = vec_a_pos
        v2 = vec_b_pos
        v3 = vec_d_pos
        
        # Offset vectors
        off_a = v1 - v0
        off_b = v2 - v0
        off_d = v3 - v0
        
        # Other vertices
        v_ab = v1 + off_b
        v_ad = v1 + off_d
        v_bd = v2 + off_d
        v_abd = v_ab + off_d
        
        # Faces
        face_back = Polygon(v3, v_ad, v_abd, v_bd, color="#ADFF2F", fill_opacity=0.1, stroke_width=1)
        face_right = Polygon(v1, v_ab, v_abd, v_ad, color="#ADFF2F", fill_opacity=0.1, stroke_width=1)
        face_top = Polygon(v2, v_ab, v_abd, v_bd, color="#ADFF2F", fill_opacity=0.1, stroke_width=1)
        
        # Edges to complete the wireframe look
        edge_1 = Line(v1, v_ad, color="#ADFF2F", stroke_width=1)
        edge_2 = Line(v2, v_bd, color="#ADFF2F", stroke_width=1)
        edge_3 = Line(v_ab, v_abd, color="#ADFF2F", stroke_width=1)
        
        cube_volume = VGroup(face_back, face_right, face_top, edge_1, edge_2, edge_3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cube_volume))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup: Return lecture to white
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Basis: The Goldilocks Set"
        lines = [
            "A basis is a perfect set of building blocks.",
            "It must span the entire vector space.",
            "Every vector in a basis must be linearly independent.",
            "It is the minimal set needed for full coverage.",
            "A basis provides efficient navigation with no redundancy."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Vector Definitions
        east_color = "#FFD700"
        north_color = "#00BFFF"
        up_color = "#ADFF2F"
        redundant_color = RED

        # Coordinate axes simulation in 2D (Perspective-like)
        origin = self.grid["D3"]
        v_east = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + RIGHT*1.2, color=east_color, buff=0)
        v_north = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + UP*1.2, color=north_color, buff=0)
        v_up = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + (RIGHT*0.5 + UP*0.5), color=up_color, buff=0)
        
        label_e = Text("East", font_size=16, color=east_color)
        label_n = Text("North", font_size=16, color=north_color)
        label_u = Text("Up", font_size=16, color=up_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label_e, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_u, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)

        basis_group = VGroup(v_east, v_north, v_up, label_e, label_n, label_u)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(v_east), Create(v_north), Create(v_up), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Write(label_e), Write(label_n), Write(label_u))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Representing "Spanning 3D volume" with a semi-transparent box or parallelogram
        plane_1 = Polygon(origin, origin + RIGHT*2, origin + RIGHT*2.5 + UP*0.5, origin + RIGHT*0.5 + UP*0.5, 
                         fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
        plane_2 = Polygon(origin, origin + UP*2, origin + RIGHT*0.5 + UP*2.5, origin + RIGHT*0.5 + UP*0.5, 
                         fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
        volume_box = VGroup(plane_1, plane_2).set_color(WHITE)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(volume_box))
        self.play(volume_box.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(0.1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Redundant Northeast vector
        v_ne = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + RIGHT*0.8 + UP*0.8, color=redundant_color, buff=0)
        label_ne = Text("Northeast", font_size=16, color=redundant_color)
        self.place_at_grid(label_ne, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(v_ne), Write(label_ne))
        self.play(Indicate(v_ne, color=RED))
        self.play(FadeOut(v_ne), FadeOut(label_ne)) # Emphasize it doesn't belong in the "Basis" set
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Minimal set: Remove 'Up' and show volume collapse
        self.play(FadeOut(v_up), FadeOut(label_u))
        collapse_msg = Text("Volume → Plane", font_size=20, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(collapse_msg, "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(volume_box.animate.set_fill(opacity=0).set_stroke(opacity=0.2), Write(collapse_msg))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Restore Basis
        self.play(FadeIn(v_up), FadeIn(label_u), FadeOut(collapse_msg), volume_box.animate.set_opacity(0.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Indicate(basis_group))
        self.play(FadeOut(volume_box))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The DNA of Linear Spaces: From Linear Combinations to Bases
outline.target_audience: University students beginning Linear Algebra or Computer Science

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
sections.content: Briefly recap vectors as 'movements' in space. Introduce the 'Linear Combination' as the fundamental operation: scaling vectors and adding them together. Explain that any vector can be scaled (stretched/shrunk) or flipped (negative scale).
sections.example: Imagine a Robot Scout that can move in two directions: Vector A (1 step East) and Vector B (1 step North). A 'Linear Combination' is like giving the robot instructions: '3 steps of A + 2 steps of B' to reach a specific coordinate.

sections.title: The Span: Reaching Every Corner
sections.content: Define 'Span' as the set of all possible points (the 'territory') reachable through linear combinations of a given set of vectors. Use 2D and 3D graphical visualizations to show how two vectors can 'paint' a whole plane.
sections.example: If our Robot Scout has Vector A (East) and Vector B (North), the 'Span' is the entire infinite flat floor. If the robot only had Vector A, its 'Span' would be just a single infinite line along the X-axis.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Trap
sections.content: Introduce Linear Dependence. If one vector can be created by a combination of the others, it adds no new 'territory' to the Span. Visually, show a third vector lying within the plane created by the first two.
sections.example: A third robot, Vector C, moves Northeast. Since Vector C = Vector A + Vector B, adding Vector C to the team doesn't let the robots reach any new spots. Vector C is 'linearly dependent' and redundant.

sections.title: Linear Independence: The Essential Team
sections.content: Contrast dependence with independence. Vectors are 'Linearly Independent' if none of them can be built from the others. Each vector provides a unique, necessary direction of movement.
sections.example: If we introduce Vector D which moves 'Up' (Z-axis) into the 3rd dimension, it cannot be made by any combination of East and North. Vector D is 'Linearly Independent' from A and B, expanding the Span from a plane to a 3D volume.

sections.title: The Basis: The Goldilocks Set
sections.content: Define a 'Basis' as the perfect set of vectors that: 1) Spans the entire space, and 2) Is linearly independent. It is the minimal set of building blocks needed to describe every point in a space without redundancy.
sections.example: In our 3D room, the set {East, North, Up} is a Basis. If you remove one, you lose a dimension (cannot Span). If you add one (like Northeast), you have redundancy (not Independent). A Basis is the 'Efficient Navigation Kit'.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
lecture_lines: Vectors represent movements or directions in space.
We can scale vectors to stretch or shrink them.
Adding scaled vectors creates a linear combination.
For example, three steps East and two steps North.
This operation combines basic movements into new paths.
animations: Show a vector arrow labeled 'A' in #FFD700 pointing East.
Stretch the vector 'A' to double its length, then flip it to point West, updating the label to 'k*A'.
Show vector 'A' (East, #FFD700) and 'B' (North, #00BFFF). Scale them to '3A' and '2B', then add them tip-to-tail to reach coordinate (3,2).

storyboard.title: The Span: Reaching Every Corner
lecture_lines: The span is the set of all reachable points.
Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane.
One vector alone only spans a single line.
animations: Show vectors 'A' (East, #FFD700) and 'B' (North, #00BFFF) at the origin.
Create many points representing linear combinations of A and B, filling a 2D plane [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/plane.svg] in #404040.
Remove vector 'B' and show the span of vector 'A' as an infinite line [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/line.svg] extending along the X-axis.

storyboard.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Trap
lecture_lines: Linear dependence means one vector is redundant.
It can be formed by combining other vectors.
Redundant vectors do not expand the existing span.
animations: Show vectors 'A' (East, #FFD700) and 'B' (North, #00BFFF) defining a horizontal plane [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/plane.svg].
Add vector 'C' in #FF4500 pointing Northeast, lying flat on the plane formed by A and B.
Demonstrate that 'C' is formed by 'A + B' tip-to-tail, highlighting that it adds no new area to the span.

storyboard.title: Linear Independence: The Essential Team
lecture_lines: Linearly independent vectors provide unique, essential directions.
No vector in the set depends on the others.
Adding an independent vector increases the dimension spanned.
animations: Show vectors 'A' (East, #FFD700) and 'B' (North, #00BFFF) on a 2D plane.
Introduce vector 'D' in #ADFF2F pointing 'Up' out of the plane.
Expand the 2D plane into a translucent 3D volume (cube) to show the new span.

storyboard.title: The Basis: The Goldilocks Set
lecture_lines: A basis is a perfect set of building blocks.
It must span the entire vector space.
Every vector in a basis must be linearly independent.
It is the minimal set needed for full coverage.
A basis provides efficient navigation with no redundancy.
animations: Show the set of vectors {East, North, Up} with colors #FFD700, #00BFFF, and #ADFF2F.
Highlight the entire 3D volume being filled by combinations of these three vectors.
Temporarily remove 'Up' to show the volume collapse to a plane, then add a redundant Northeast vector and highlight it in red.
